findings.evidence: Line 404 `(∃ f, f.twist = 2 ∧ O = {f})` together with `LightConeField.twist_eq_two_iff` (line 231) `f = quark .bad ∨ f = quarkBar .bad ∨ ...`; `quarkNumber_quark = 1` (line 207) shows these singletons are quark fields, not field strengths.
findings.fix: Restrict the sentence to the field-strength singletons, e.g. "The single field-strength cases (`F^{+-}`, `F^{ij}`, `F^{-i}`) are colour octets and drop out of any gauge-invariant operator; they are kept because colour is not recorded in the field content."
findings.issue: "The single-field cases are colour octets and drop out of any gauge-invariant operator" is false for the general classifications listed just above: `twist_eq_two_iff` (line 403) admits the single-field case `O = {quark .bad}` / `{quarkBar .bad}`, and `twist_eq_one_iff` (line 392) `O = {quark .good}` — colour triplets, not octets.

findings.evidence: Line 37–40: "a derivative has mass dimension `1`, so `D^+`, `D^i` and `D^-` would carry twist zero, one and two" — a `D^+` insertion breaks both `card_le_twist` and `twist_eq_zero_iff` for physical operators.
findings.fix: Add "derivative-free" to these five docstrings and to the `card_le_twist` bullet in the Main statements block (line 61), matching the wording already used at lines 391/401/417.
findings.issue: `card_le_twist` ("An operator has twist at least its number of fields"), `twist_eq_zero_iff` (line 369, "Only the empty field content, the identity operator, has twist zero"), `twist_eq_card_iff` (line 375), `le_twist_of_mem` (line 358) and `twist_mono` (line 363) assert claims about "an operator" without the derivative-free qualifier, yet all fail once covariant derivatives are admitted (the module itself says at lines 37–40 that `D^+` has twist zero). The classification lemmas at lines 391, 401, 417 do carry the qualifier.

summary: Module docstring and per-declaration docstrings are substantive, mathematical and free of roadmap/process narrative, and every definition and main theorem is documented. Two prose claims are inaccurate: the colour-octet remark is false for the single-quark-field cases of the general classifications, and the derivative-free caveat is applied inconsistently to statements that are equally derivative-sensitive.
